2] This is the first application filed by the applicant  482 of the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023/Section 438 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 for grant of anticipatory bail as he is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.732/2025 registered at Police Station Khajrana, District Indore for the offence punishable under Sections 294,
323, 376, 376(2)(n), 458 & 506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
sentences._hearing_file: Arjun vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 26 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: 3] The allegation against the applicant is of rape on the pretext of marriage, and it is also alleged that the applicant had obtained objectionable photos and videos of the complainant, and he was also blackmailing her.
sentences._hearing_file: Arjun vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 26 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: 4] Counsel for the applicant has submitted that the present FIR has been lodged on 13.09.2025 in respect of the incident which took place between 01.08.2018 and 01.06.2024, which in itself is sufficient to hold that it is a NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:28764 2 MCRC-43788-2025 case of consent and only on account of a dispute between the parties, the FIR has been lodged.
sentences._hearing_file: Arjun vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 26 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is also submitted that the dispute is in respect of the money transaction between the applicant and the father of the prosecutrix/complainant, which occurred on 12.09.2025 at around 9:30 PM when the applicant had gone to the house of the complainant, where the father of the complainant caused a gunshot injury to the applicant, which also stuck in his right hand, and when the FIR of the same was lodged on 13.09.2025 at around 3:55 PM, the present FIR has been lodged on 13.09.2025 itself at 11 O' clock in the night.
sentences._hearing_file: Arjun vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 26 September, 2025.json

sentences.text:
Counsel has also drawn the attention of this Court to the various Arjun vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 26 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77145297/
1 photographs and WhatsApp chats as also the monetary transaction between the parties wherein the applicant has given various amounts to the complainant, which according to the applicant is more than Rs.6 lakh.

entities.text: Arjun vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh

sentences._hearing_file: Arjun vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 26 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: Thus, it is prayed that the application be allowed.
sentences._hearing_file: Arjun vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 26 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: 5] Counsel for the objector, on the other hand, has vehemently opposed the prayer, and has drawn the attention of this Court to the WhatsApp chats.
sentences._hearing_file: Arjun vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 26 September, 2025.json

sentences.text:
It is also submitted that the monetary transaction was indeed going on between the parties, but that has nothing to do with the allegations of rape against the applicant, and only because of the obscene messages sent by the applicant to the complainant, which enraged his father,
resulting in the shooting incident.
sentences._hearing_file: Arjun vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 26 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: Thus, it is submitted that no case for grant of anticipatory bail is made out.
sentences._hearing_file: Arjun vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 26 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: 6] Having considered the rival submissions, perusal of the case-diary as also the various documents filed by the parties on record, it is found that the applicant and the prosecutrix were having cordial relationship for quite some time, however, the same appears to have gone sore, and apparently monetary NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:28764 3 MCRC-43788-2025 transactions also took place between the parties, resulting in some disputes, in which the applicant also got shot by the father of the complainant/prosecutrix, regarding which he filed the FIR at Crime No.730 of 2025, whereas the FIR lodged by the prosecutrix is at Crime No.732 of 2025 at the same police station on 13.09.2025.
sentences._hearing_file: Arjun vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 26 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: In such circumstances, this Court is of the considered opinion that the custodial interrogation of the applicant, who is already injured, does not appear necessary.
sentences._hearing_file: Arjun vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 26 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: 7] Accordingly, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.
sentences._hearing_file: Arjun vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 26 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is directed that in the event of arrest, applicant shall be released on bail, upon his executing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (rupees twenty five thousand only) and furnishing one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer (Investigating Officer).
sentences._hearing_file: Arjun vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 26 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: The applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by a Police Officer, as and when required.
sentences._hearing_file: Arjun vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 26 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: He shall further abide by the other conditions enumerated in Sub Section (2) of Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
sentences._hearing_file: Arjun vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 26 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: 8] Accordingly, MCRC stands allowed.

sentences.text: Appellant has filed this appeal against the judgment dated 25.02.2025 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge, Khachrod, District Ujjain (M.P.) in ST No.33/2023 whereby the learned trial Court has convicted the appellant under section 376(1) of the IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for 10 years with fine of Rs.10,000/- with further default stipulations for committing penetrative sexual assault with a child (PW-1) aged 16 years 7 months and 2 days.

sentences.text: Counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant is innocent and falsely been implicated in the case.

sentences.text: Hence prayed for suspension of sentence and release of the appellant on bail.

sentences.text: Counsel for the State has opposed the application.

sentences.text: The age of the child is proved through birth certificate (Exhibit- P/5).

sentences.text: The act of penetrative sexual assault is proved through DNA report (Exhibit-P/5) which found the presence of "Y" male DNA profile on the underwear, public hair and vaginal slide collected during medical 2 CRA-3311-2025 examination of child (PW-1).

sentences._hearing_file: Arjun vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 2 December, 2025.json

3] The allegation against the applicant is of rape on the pretext of marriage, and it is also alleged that the applicant had obtained objectionable photos and videos of the complainant, and he was also blackmailing her.
opennyai_summary.26_September_2025__arguments:
It is also submitted that the dispute is in respect of the money transaction between the applicant and the father of the prosecutrix/complainant, which occurred on 12.09.2025 at around 9:30 PM when the applicant had gone to the house of the complainant, where the father of the complainant caused a gunshot injury to the applicant, which also stuck in his right hand, and when the FIR of the same was lodged on 13.09.2025 at around 3:55 PM, the present FIR has been lodged on 13.09.2025 itself at 11 O' clock in the night.
It is also submitted that the monetary transaction was indeed going on between the parties, but that has nothing to do with the allegations of rape against the applicant, and only because of the obscene messages sent by the applicant to the complainant, which enraged his father,
resulting in the shooting incident.
Thus, it is submitted that no case for grant of anticipatory bail is made out.
opennyai_summary.26_September_2025__ANALYSIS:
6] Having considered the rival submissions, perusal of the case-diary as also the various documents filed by the parties on record, it is found that the applicant and the prosecutrix were having cordial relationship for quite some time, however, the same appears to have gone sore, and apparently monetary NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:28764 3 MCRC-43788-2025 transactions also took place between the parties, resulting in some disputes, in which the applicant also got shot by the father of the complainant/prosecutrix, regarding which he filed the FIR at Crime No.730 of 2025, whereas the FIR lodged by the prosecutrix is at Crime No.732 of 2025 at the same police station on 13.09.2025.
In such circumstances, this Court is of the considered opinion that the custodial interrogation of the applicant, who is already injured, does not appear necessary.
opennyai_summary.26_September_2025__decision:
7] Accordingly, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

8] Accordingly, MCRC stands allowed.
